title: Time series change points
text: mcp implements AR MA generalized ARMA (GARMA) recurrence response-family link scale. b_t ordinary regression predictor segment formulas \eta_t predictor including serial dependence, \begin{aligned} \text{AR}_t &= \sum_{j=1}^{p} \phi_{j,t} \left[g(y^*_{t-j}) - b_{t-j}\right] \\ \text{MA}_t &= \sum_{k=1}^{q} \theta_{k,t} \left[g(y^*_{t-k}) - \eta_{t-k}\right] \\ \eta_t &= b_t + \text{AR}_t + \text{MA}_t \end{aligned} \phi_{j,t} lag-j autoregressive (AR) coefficient time t, \theta_{k,t} lag-k moving-average (MA) coefficient time t, g(\cdot) link function, y^* boundary-constrained observation. Thus ar() uses lagged link-scale residuals relative ordinary regression, ma() uses lagged one-step innovations. mcp regression change points coefficients \phi_{j,t} \theta_{k,t}. See applied examples. Unavailable lags beginning series contribute zero. recurrence used JAGS, fitted values, predictions, log likelihoods, fresh-series simulation. key feature recurrence AR/MA memory flows continuously across change points: order-N component new segment, last N observations change point input first \eta_t new segment, weighted new segment’s AR/MA parameters. GARMA currently supports default links gaussian() (identity), binomial() (logit), poisson() (log), negbinomial() (log). bernoulli() non-default links rejected now. Warning: AR MA coefficients modeled directly jointly constrained stationary invertible regions. higher-order terms ar(2), independently bounded coefficients can violate usual root conditions. Understanding mcp formulas: Parameter names Intercept_i (intercepts), cp_i (change points), x_i (slopes), ar*/ma* (autocorrelation), sigma_* (Gaussian residual standard deviation). change point model basically ifelse model order constraints change points. Generate data supported models using fit$simulate(). See examples , e.g., mcp_example("demo")$example_code. Supported families link functions: mcp currently supports specific combinations families (gaussian(), binomial(), bernoulli(), poisson(), negbinomial()) link functions (identity, logit, probit, log). using informative priors incorporate expert knowledge. Use binomial(link = "logit") binomial change points mcp. Also relevant bernoulli(link = "logit"). Use negbinomial(link = "log") poisson(link = "log"). Read Poisson negative binomial change points mcp. Get results linear-predictor (link) scale rather response scale using plot(fit, scale = "linear") fitted(fit, scale = "linear"). Model comparison hypothesis testing: Leave-One-Cross-Validation using loo(fit) loo::loo_compare(loo1, loo2). Compute Savage-Dickey density ratios using hypothesis(fit, "cp_1 = 40"). Group-level (random) effects: Model group-level intercepts, slopes, change points using (1|id), (condition||id), +(condition|id). Get posteriors using ranef(fit). Plot using plot(fit, facet_by = "my_group") plot_pars(fit, pars = "group", type = "dens_overlay", ncol = 3). Default priors bound group-specific change points relative adjacent population-level change points. Modeling autoregression distributional parameters like Gaussian residual standard deviation: ~ 0 + sigma(1) models intercept change standard deviation. ~ 0 + sigma(0 + x) models increasing/decreasing standard deviation. Explicit sigma() formulas use log link, coefficients log-SD scale. ~ ar(N) models Nth order autoregression residuals. ~ar(N, 0 + x) models increasing/decreasing autocorrelation. y | weights(w) (y | trials(N) + weights(w)) specifies observation log-likelihood weights across families, brms. can provide complete models distributional parameters (currently sigma(), shape(), mu()) time-series (ar() ma()). example, ~ x + sigma(1 + x:condition) models abrupt change followed -condition slopes variance. Get fitted predicted values intervals: fitted(fit) predict(fit) take many arguments predict -sample --sample values intervals. Forecasting prior knowledge future change points. Using priors: See priors fit$prior prior_summary(fit) set priors using mcp(..., prior = list(cp_1 = "dnorm(0, 1)", cp_2 = "dunif(0, 45)"). One change point uniform default prior. ideal default prior multiple change points cp_i = "dirichlet(1)" simplex equidistant beta distributions, samples inefficiently, mcp defaults approximation using truncated Student-t priors centered minimum x. Informativeness increases number change points increase. Fix parameters specific values using cp_1 = 45 share parameters segments using slope_1 = "slope_2". Truncate priors using T(lower, upper), e.g., Intercept_1 = "dnorm(0, 1) T(0, )". mcp adds ordering bounds population-level change-point priors. Users can override . prior predictive checks using mcp(model, data, sample = "prior") |> plot(). Missing responses posterior imputation: Missing responses sampled JAGS retained matching posterior draws. Use fitted(fit) |> filter(.na(y)) expected responses predict(fit) |> filter(.na(y)) posterior imputations. plotting missing responses, asking probabilistic questions , etc. Tips, tricks, debugging Speed fitting using future::plan(future::multisession, workers = 3), /fewer iterations, mcp(..., warmup = 500). text: mcp model continuous predictor \(x\), segment 1 (\(x \le \Delta_1\)) standard regression model intercept defined \(x = 0\): $$\eta_{1, } = f_1(x_i, \mathbf{\beta}_1) = \beta_{1,0} + \beta_{1,1} x_i + \dots$$ subsequent segments \(k \\{2, \dots, K\}\), change point \(\Delta_{k-1}\) marks onset new segment. model defines segment-local predictor \(X_{k,}\) measured segment onset \(\Delta_{k-1}\) capped segment end \(\Delta_k\): $$X_{k,} = \min(x_i, \Delta_k) - \Delta_{k-1}$$ \(\Delta_K = \max(\mathbf{x})\). local predictor \(X_{k,}\) zero segment onset (\(x_i \le \Delta_{k-1}\)) plateaus \(\Delta_k - \Delta_{k-1}\) \(x_i \ge \Delta_k\). Joined (continuous) segments (~ 0 + x) joined models, segment \(k \ge 2\) intercept specifies new segment slope \(\beta_{k,1}\): $$\eta_i = \eta_{1,}(X_{1,}) + \sum_{k=2}^K [x_i \ge \Delta_{k-1}] \cdot \beta_{k,1} X_{k,}$$ \(X_{1,} = \min(x_i, \Delta_1)\). earlier segments plateau boundary values, expectation automatically continuous across change points without requiring parameter constraints. joined disjoined segments, slope intercept parameters absolute values (differences relative previous segment). Disjoined (discontinuous) segments (~ 1 + x) segment \(k\) contains explicit intercept (\(\beta_{k,0}\)), introduces step change \(x_i = \Delta_{k-1}\) previous segments truncated \([x_i < \Delta_{k-1}]\). Extended formulas model features Distributional regression: Model residual variance distributional parameters across segments, e.g., ~ sigma(1 + x) ~ shape(1). Time-series residuals: Model serial dependence using ar(p) ma(q) terms generalized link-scale recurrence spans continuously across change points. Group-level effects: Add hierarchical (random) intercepts, slopes, change points, e.g., ~ 1 + (1|id) 1 + (1|id) ~ 0 + x. Model comparison hypothesis testing: Compare models using LOO-CV (loo(), waic()) test directional point-null hypotheses (hypothesis()) using Savage-Dickey density ratios. title: mcp 0.4.0
text: Multiple regression: mcp now supports several continuous predictors, categorical predictors, interactions, etc. terms RHS. E.g., ~ 1 + x + x:group + sigma(1 + group) + ar(2, 0 + z). Basically, now aims “feels” like lm() glm() distributional parameter segment. Explore ex = mcp_example("multiple") see action. Default priors generally align brms, adjustments accommodate change-point model. Group-level effects RHS: Predictor formulas now support group-level effects (random effects) using familiar lme4 brms syntax. (1 | group) specifies group-level intercept, (1 + x || group) (factor || group) support independent coefficients, including slopes factors. also works inside distributional formulas sigma(1 + (factor || id)). ar(), effect carries later segments redefined disabled (0 | group). See mcp_example("group_mu") worked example. Correlated multi-coefficient terms yet supported. Native feel: mcpfits now work natively R generics, posterior tidybayes posterior draw prediction API. Changes include: summary(fit) now reports rank-normalized split-rhat, ess_bulk, ess_tail posterior central quantile intervals instead HDIs. Adding as_draws(fit), as_draws_df(fit), tidy_draws(fit), ndraws(fit), rstantools linpred/epred, etc. full S3 generic registration posterior, rstantools, tidybayes (spread_draws(), gather_draws()). Per-draw methods (summary = FALSE fitted(), predict(), residuals(), log_lik()) now return dot-prefixed columns (.epred, .prediction, .residual, .loglik) tidybayes / ggdist compatibility. nsamples soft-deprecated favor ndraws; which_y deprecated favor dpar. Added R generics mcpfits: formula(fit), family(fit), model.frame(fit), nobs(fit), vcov(fit), confint(fit). Fits now also store proper matched $call. Printed summaries now report posterior sd new layout. Negative binomial, offset(), GARMA: can now mcp(..., family = negbinomial()). NB (Poisson) can now model rates exposure offset() now supported formulas - also families. Autoregression (ar()) generalized GARMA link-scale residuals Gaussian, binomial, Poisson, negative-binomial models default links, using ar(..., boundary = 0.1) default keep zero boundary counts finite. Added moving-average terms ma(q), can used alone combined ar(p) segment. Missing response imputation: Missing responses now retained posterior JAGS imputations. predict(fit) |> filter(.na(y)) can used see imputed values - similarly fitted(). supports AR/MA . Missing values AR/MA supported log_lik(), loo(), waic() throw informative error. See details new vignette/article missing data.

title: mcp 0.4.0
text: mcp v0.4 major breaking change aim remaining relatively stable going forward towards version 1.0. Although lot updated, parameter estimates v0.4.0 remain practically identical previous public release (v0.3.4). Deprecation detections added reach 1.0. Renamed parameters consistent brms: int_i –> Intercept_i; x_1_E2 –> xE2_1; x_1_sin –> sinx_1, etc. summary(), fixef(), ranef(), prior_summary(), everything else now return rows canonical order instead previous incidental (near-alphabetical) order. Use verbose = TRUE summary(), fixef(), ranef() include segment dpar columns. Rhat renamed rhat summary(), fixef(), ranef(), match posterior standard. plot() now split plot() plotting full fits plot_dpar() plots one distributional parameter (mu, sigma, shape, ar1, etc.). argument order changed . new coloring function (plot(fit, color_by = "column")) particularly useful models include categorical predictors rhs group-level effects. See mcp_example("group_mu") worked example. hypothesis() now restricts equality tests simple parameter contrasts gives clearer guidance Savage-Dickey Bayes factors. Non-linear transformations hypotheses like x_1 / x_2 = 1 previously run, even though Savage-Dickey support . Equality tests now return p = NA Bayes factor model comparison, posterior parameter probability. Density estimates robust, warn evaluating Savage-Dickey Bayes factors default priors, warn sparse tails. fixef() now reports population-level effects mu (primary response parameter), excluding change points, distributional parameters, AR/MA parameters, group-effect SDs. Use summary(fit) get parameters. fit$pars removed. Use mcp_pars(fit) canonical table model parameters mcp_columns(fit) resolved data-column roles, including automatically chosen par_x. general, renamed "varying" "group". old "varying" selector remains deprecated alias. established varying = method argument remains unchanged now. y | weights(w) now specifies brms-aligned observation log-likelihood weights across supported families (gaussian(), binomial(), bernoulli(), poisson(), negbinomial()), rather Gaussian-precision weights (previously scaled residual SD sigma / sqrt(w)). Predictive draws expectations now use distribution parameters directly log_lik() multiplies observation log-densities w. AR MA intercepts now zero-centered, regularizing dnorm(0, 0.5) T(-1, 1) priors, replacing independent uniform priors. categorical contrasts numeric slopes now use modest normal priors instead heavy-tailed Student-t priors. Coefficients remain direct jointly constrained stationary invertible regions. Gaussian models explicit sigma() formula now model residual standard deviation log link, brms. Models without explicit sigma() unchanged: sigma_1 remains residual SD response-scale half-Student-t prior. Formula transformations now use original predictor values, lm(), glm(), brms. Previously, transformations change-point predictor sin(x) exp(x) restarted segment onset. Bare par_x polynomial bases (par_x^2) remain segment-local support joined segment shapes. Corrected JAGS translation prior scales. ddexp() dlogis() now convert conventional scale inverse scale rather inverse variance; exported sd_to_prec() helper soft-deprecated prior translation now internal, sampler-specific step. Group-level change points (1|id) remain exactly zero-centered identify population-level change points support efficient sampling. models multiple group-level change points, realized locations now constrained remain ordered. Read vignette group-level effects. sampling, mcp() now verifies population- group-level change points strictly ordered every draw population-level change points lie within observed predictor range. ordering broken, wrong segments apply. Parallel sampling now controlled exclusively active future plan. cores argument mcp() deprecated ignored, remains available backwards compatibility. Use future::plan(future::multisession, workers = 3) calling mcp() sample chains parallel, future::plan(future::sequential) shut workers.
